definitions: To scratch or scrape a surface, a wound, or a lottery ticket.
Familier: to gain or squeeze out a small amount of something, such as time, money, or votes.
Usage note: In everyday speech, "gratter" is commonly used to mean "to itch" or "to feel scratchy," as in "ça me gratte," whereas formal usage prefers "démanger."
examples: Il a passé dix minutes à gratter le givre sur son pare-brise avant de prendre la route.
He spent ten minutes scraping the frost off his windshield before hitting the road.
Les négociateurs espèrent encore gratter quelques millions d'euros dans le budget de l'an prochain.
The negotiators still hope to squeeze out a few million euros in next year's budget.
Ce pull en laine me gratte tellement le cou que je ne peux pas le supporter.
This wool sweater makes my neck itch so much that I can't stand it.

The decision remains valid, notwithstanding any subsequent appeal.

definitions: To paint a surface, object, or artwork with paint.

Usage note: Use the preposition "en" before the color when specifying the result of painting a surface, rather than a bare adjective as in English.
examples: Mon grand-père peignait des paysages maritimes dans son atelier du grenier.

Dans ce roman, l'autrice peignait avec finesse les tensions d'une petite ville de province.
In this novel, the author deftly portrayed the tensions of a small provincial town.
Nous avons décidé de peindre le salon en blanc pour rendre la pièce plus lumineuse.
We decided to paint the living room white to make the room brighter.

definitions: Indicates that a situation or fact is unchangeable or obvious, often with a tone of resignation; umgangssprachlich, equivalent to just or simply.
Usage note: Very common in everyday speech and informal prose, especially in southern Germany, Austria, and Switzerland; in more formal writing or northern usage, eben is often preferred.
examples: Der Zug hat Verspätung, da müssen wir halt warten.
The train is delayed, so we'll just have to wait.
Wenn dir das Buch nicht gefällt, liest du halt ein anderes.
If you don't like the book, just read another one.
